actualKallistoImport.scope: Actual upstream kallisto output import, not differential-expression inference on three transcripts

actualKallistoFixture.source: Actual unmodified upstream kallisto0.52.0 Linux executable output, using exact fixtures from released Workbench kallisto1.0.1. This is tximport parser/estimates compatibility, not a differential expression experiment.

No GUI, clinical, repeated-measure or whole-transcriptome memory/cancellation validation.

historicalLocalGraphDiagnostic.interpretation: Five of six passed on this final ZIP; the strict duplicate-import assertion found only temporary extracted files reappearing after cleanup in the managed Linux workspace. No installed file changed or disappeared. This failure is preserved. Both exact-final Windows graph/archive suites pass all six cases, including duplicate-import immutability.

historicalFailedDevelopmentRuns.finding: An incorrect R curl diagnostic function failed before scientific tests.
R startup required a space-free R_TempDir; fixed by owned scratch with existing short alias or explicit scratch root.
A missing summary-list closing parenthesis caused a parse failure after model execution; corrected before the final pack.
Thirteen of fourteen tests passed; incorrect raw-vs-tximport baseMean equality was replaced by strict independently called upstream API comparisons without algorithm or fixture changes.

pack.name: DESeq2 differential expression
pack.description: Bulk RNA differential expression with DESeq2, tximport and private R. Raw gene matrices, featureCounts and kallisto sample fan-in. Workbench 0.6.0 or newer.

normalizationOracleCorrection.explanation: DESeq2 centers tximport normalization factors to geometric mean 1 while ordinary matrix size factors are not recentered. Cross-mode baseMean equality is therefore not the correct oracle. Every inferential column is independently checked against its own unwrapped upstream API at relative tolerance 1e-10, 300 genes per mode, 600 gene comparisons. Raw featureCounts equality and planted-effect/null assertions remain strict.

scientificScope: Three operations: raw integer gene-count matrix; 4-64 single-sample featureCounts gene tables; 4-64 kallisto abundance.tsv files with complete exact transcript-to-gene mapping. Released metrics ports require additional adapter semantic validation.

Explicit sample identifiers, condition, biological replicate, optional batch and fan-in input_index establish input order. At least two distinct biological replicates per condition, full-rank design and two residual degrees of freedom are enforced. Conditions and optional additive batch are bounded choices, never arbitrary R code.

Actual serial DESeq2 Wald inference uses median-of-ratios normalization, parametric dispersion request with upstream fallback, independent filtering, Cook cutoff and BH adjustment. Kallisto uses tximport countsFromAbundance=no and DESeqDataSetFromTximport length offsets. No automatic outlier replacement or fold-change shrinkage.

Deterministic 300-gene/six-sample fixture recovers all 12 planted positive and 12 negative effects; pinned upstream output also has four incidental null discoveries, totaling 13 positive and 15 negative significant genes. This is a regression baseline, not FDR calibration or a power benchmark.

Independent direct upstream matrix and tximport reference results agree across 600 gene comparisons at tolerance 1e-10. A separate actual upstream kallisto three-transcript plaintext fixture tests import compatibility only, not differential inference on three transcripts.

All-gene results preserve NA and prefiltered status, imported/normalized counts, exact sample-labeled model matrix, PCA/MA PDFs, methods, session/runtime versions, commands and input provenance. Tests cover actual model output, malformed inputs, batch confounding, insufficient replication, offsets, private startup and unchanged installed/user files.
boundaries: Native installation checks use the actual released Workbench bridge, importer and scientific runner. Graph/archive tests use a checked copy callback for folder publication and do not themselves execute scientific programs or the native importer. Installed private-R scientific regressions are separate.

Research/teaching validation with deterministic synthetic fixtures; no clinical, diagnostic, regulatory, institutional approval or large-cohort performance claim. No interactive desktop GUI, cancellation, Unicode/long-path or firewall test. Ordinary and space-containing ASCII Windows paths were exercised.

The pack supports independent bulk-RNA samples and fixed condition or additive batch+condition designs. It does not expose paired/repeated-measures, continuous covariates, interactions, single-cell models or arbitrary formulas.

Numeric integer/header validation cannot prove counts were never normalized or that asserted biological replicates are independent. Users must provide genuine raw gene counts or compatible kallisto estimates, matched annotations and biologically appropriate design.

Private pinned R and Python require no system installation, runtime package downloads or user library. R requires a space-free scratch path: use the OS temp short alias or an explicit existing writable scratch-root folder. No administrator rights or drive mappings are used; normal completion deletes only the owned scratch child.

Each retained run expands a 268007078-byte private R/package tree containing 6864 files, plus staged inputs and scientific outputs. Pack limits are 64 samples, 250000 genes and at least 20 genes retained; local memory/disk remain limiting.

The separate runtime source companion includes 59 upstream archives and 230 pinned source/recipe files for the conservative Rtools base-library/compiler-runtime and Tcl/Tk closure. This is corresponding-source coverage, not proof of bit-identical rebuilding of upstream DLLs; documented general build prerequisites and base-only target apply.
Offline inventory and SHA verification establish integrity, not publisher identity. Signed-catalogue trust deployment is a separate project task.
